statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the number of equivalence classes of the following relation on the index set {0,1,...,n-1}: indices i and k are related if and only if, for every lowercase letter c, the number of even positions j with 0 <= j < m and words[i][j] = c equals the corresponding number for words[k], and the number of odd positions j with 0 <= j < m and words[i][j] = c equals the corresponding number for words[k]. Equivalently, r is the number of distinct pairs (E,O), where E is the multiset of even-indexed characters of some words[i] and O is the multiset of odd-indexed characters of that same words[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, and every byte of every words[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z'.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail (no panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow).
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, and every byte of every words[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, and every byte of every words[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= D, where D is the number of distinct byte strings among words[0], words[1], ..., words[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, and every byte of every words[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if every two indices i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n are special-equivalent; here special-equivalent means that for every lowercase letter c, the number of occurrences of c at even positions of words[i] equals that of words[j], and the number of occurrences of c at odd positions of words[i] equals that of words[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, and every byte of every words[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z'.

statement: If for every pair of distinct indices i,j with 0 <= i < j < n, words[i] and words[j] are not special-equivalent (that is, for some lowercase letter c their even-position counts differ or their odd-position counts differ), then whenever the function returns a result r, r = n.
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, and every byte of every words[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of distinct byte values among the characters words[0][0], words[1][0], ..., words[n-1][0].
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, every byte is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z', and m = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of distinct two-byte strings among words[0], words[1], ..., words[n-1], i.e. the number of distinct pairs (words[i][0], words[i][1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, every byte is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z', and m = 2.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on words and r' on words', r' = r if w is special-equivalent to at least one words[i] with 0 <= i < n, and r' = r + 1 otherwise. Here special-equivalent means the even-position and odd-position letter counts of w equal those of words[i] for every lowercase letter.
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, every byte is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z', and n < 1000. Let w be any byte string of length m with lowercase letters, and let words' be the array of length n+1 obtained by appending w after all words.

statement: Suppose there is a bijection p on {0,1,...,n-1} such that words'[i] is byte-for-byte equal to words[p(i)] for every i < n. Whenever the function returns r on words and r' on words', r = r'.
preconditions: Let words and words' both satisfy the common preconditions with the same n = len(words) = len(words') and the same m = len(words[0]) = len(words'[0]): 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, all strings have length m, and all bytes are ASCII lowercase 'a'..'z'.

statement: Suppose that for every i < n, words'[i] and words[i] are special-equivalent, meaning that for every lowercase letter c the number of occurrences of c at even positions of words'[i] equals that of words[i], and the number of occurrences of c at odd positions of words'[i] equals that of words[i]. Whenever the function returns r on words and r' on words', r = r'.
preconditions: Let words and words' both satisfy the common preconditions with the same n = len(words) = len(words') and the same m = len(words[0]) = len(words'[0]): 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, all strings have length m, and all bytes are ASCII lowercase 'a'..'z'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a set R of exactly r indices with 0 <= i < n such that: (1) for any two distinct indices i,k in R, words[i] and words[k] are not special-equivalent; and (2) for every index k with 0 <= k < n, there is an index i in R such that words[k] and words[i] are special-equivalent. Special-equivalent has the usual meaning: equal counts of every lowercase letter at even positions and equal counts of every lowercase letter at odd positions.
preconditions: Let n = len(words) and m = len(words[0]). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 20, every words[i] has length m, and every byte of every words[i] is an ASCII lowercase letter 'a'..'z'.
